the development of a low power and area efficient error detection logic for inexact LZA in floating point units.
the development of a low power error detection circuit in inexact LZA.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed design is a novel low power and area error detection logic for inexact LZA in floating point addition unit which reduces the delay introduced by normalization.

the proposed LZA algorithm and error detection logic reduces the delay of the normalization unit in floating point addition by 30% 35% and 40% 45% respectively when compared to that of general LZAs and error detection circuit.
the proposed design is a novel design which reduces the area and power consumption of the error detection logic in inexact LZA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have implemented the error detection circuit in parallel with adders and LZA and the proposed error detection logic consumes less power when compared with that implemented in serial.
we have proposed a novel error detection logic for inexact LZA.
the proposed LZA with error detection logic is implemented in 65nm CMOS technology and it consumes only 1.2mW of power with a delay of 0.8ns.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed design can be used in any inexact LZA algorithm and can be implemented in a single clock cycle.
the error detection logic can be implemented in parallel with the LZA logic.
, by using an inexact LZA, the critical path delay can be reduced by 10% and the area and power consumption are reduced by 35% to 39% and by 44% to 48% respectively.
